subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Plastic: The Material That Won't Go Away
description: One-minute skill: Plastic: The Material That Won't Go Away.

hook.text: Humans have produced 8.3 billion tons of plastic since 1950. Only 9% has been recycled.

buildup.text: Plastics are long-chain polymers made from petroleum. They can be molded, stretched, and formed into almost anything.

discovery.text: Leo Baekeland invented Bakelite in 1907 — the first fully synthetic plastic. It couldn't melt once set.

twist.text: Plastic's greatest strength is its greatest flaw. It's durable, cheap, and lasts for 500 years in a landfill.

climax.text: Engineers now develop bioplastics from corn starch and algae. Some decompose in months, not centuries.

punchline.text: The miracle material has a 500-year hangover.

quiz.question: What percentage of all plastic ever produced has been recycled?
options: About 35%, mostly in Europe and Japan
About 9%, with most ending up in landfills or the environment
About 50%, thanks to recent recycling programs
